newsitem.title: UK: Disciplinary hearing opens on "absent" Barings man.
newsitem.headline: Disciplinary hearing opens on "absent" Barings man.

text.p: An independent disciplinary tribunal opened on Monday into charges brought by Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) against Ian Hopkins, formerly head of treasury and risk at Barings, the SFA said.

Hopkins was among a group former Barings executives charged by the SFA for their part in the downfall of the investment bank which collapsed nearly two years ago after Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson ran up debts of almost $1.4 billion in unauthorised derivatives trades.
Hopkins has consistently refused to accept the validity of the SFA charges and will not appear before the tribunal or be legally represented.

The Authority's case will be put by Presiley Baxendale QC, a prominent barrister retained by the SFA at the outset of its investigation into the Barings affair, before the tribunal chaired by Judge Colin Kolbert.
Kolbert also headed the tribunal into the case of Ron Baker, head of financial products at Barings, who last year was reprimanded after being cleared of most of the charges brought against him.
Baker has launched an appeal against the reprimand.

An SFA spokesman said the current tribunal would hear the SFA's case and will then, in the absence of Hopkins, take into account his statements to the SFA and those made in public before reaching its decision.

Hopkins told a parliamentary committee investigation into Barings last year that his attempts to alert more senior Barings staff to potential problems had failed and painted a picture of culture clashes between the traditional Barings banking activities and its newer securities activities.
In the official Singaporean report into the Barings affair, executives of the bank were criticised for not heeding Hopkins's warnings.
"In our view, the collapse might have been averted if Mr Hopkins's concerns had been taken seriously, and acted upon promptly and effectively," the Singapore inspectors said.
